answer: Coordination-Nadir Pricing. Each identity posts a small per-epoch deposit; agents in a declared coordination group pay a shared fee equal to the group's marginal size, so the fee hits its nadir only when membership matches declared intent. A group exceeding its declared cap triggers a proportional surcharge on every member. Sybils must fund each identity's deposit and surcharge, and the marginal fee rises with every added identity, so N fakes cost roughly N squared. This willow-thin signal of over-coordination is cheap to carry for honest groups, punitive for attackers.
